facts.content: Patient presents with a severe headache with visual changes.
facts.source_text: CC: Severe headache with visual changes

facts.content: The patient reports a sudden onset headache that began this morning on the left side of the head.
facts.source_text: Sudden onset headache began this morning, L side of head

facts.content: The headache pain is rated 6 out of 10 and did not respond to paracetamol.
The headache is accompanied by blurred vision, zigzag lines, and dizziness.
facts.source_text: Accompanied by blurred vision, zigzag lines, dizziness

facts.content: The patient has experienced nausea and vomited twice.
The patient expresses fear of having a brain tumor or stroke.
facts.source_text: Concerns: Fear of brain tumor or stroke

facts.content: The patient has a history of kidney stones.
The patient takes no regular medications.
The patient has no known drug allergies.
The patient's mother has migraines.
The patient's mother has hypothyroidism.
No neurological symptoms are reported on examination.
The patient's walking ability is intact.
The working diagnosis is a possible migraine.
The possible migraine is supported by unilateral headache, visual disturbances, nausea or vomiting, and dizziness.
facts.source_text: Symptoms: Unilateral headache, visual disturbances, nausea/vomiting, dizziness

facts.content: The patient is advised to take ibuprofen and an antiemetic.
The patient is recommended to drink a sugary, carbonated drink.
Consider using Migraleve if symptoms persist.
Schedule a follow-up appointment for a full neurological examination if there is no improvement.
facts.source_text: Schedule follow-up for full neurological exam if no improvement

facts.content: The patient is instructed to monitor symptoms and cancel the appointment if improvement is noted.
facts.source_text: Patient to monitor symptoms and cancel appointment if improvement noted
